newsitem.title: CANADA: RTRS-Barrick and Placer remain keen on Busang gold deposit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Barrick and Placer remain keen on Busang gold deposit.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Wednesday that it met with Barrick Gold Corp and the secretary general of the Indonesian Ministry of Mines and Energy in Jakarta.

In a brief statement, Bre-X said agreement had been reached "on matters raised by the Indonesian Ministry of Mines and Energy" outlined in a statement issued by Bre-X on November 26, but several issues remained outstanding.
No new deadline to reach an agreement with Barrick had been set by the ministry yet, Bre-X said. It said it expected clarification from the ministry on the outstanding issues.
No one at Bre-X would add details.

Bre-X said on November 26 that the Indonesian government advised it to negotiate a joint venture with Barrick, with Barrick getting 75 percent of Bre-X's stake in the huge Busang gold deposit in Indonesia and Bre-X getting 25 percent.
The Indonesian government also asked the companies to consider giving the government a 10 percent stake.
The government set a deadline of December 4.

Indonesian officials told Reuters in Jakarta on Wednesday that if no agreement was reached, "the government will take the necessary and appropriate action...to expedite the development of Busang's resources."
In Vancouver, Placer Dome Inc said it still hoped to be allowed to partner Bre-X Minerals Ltd in the development of Busang after news that Barrick was still seeking to finalize a deal with Bre-X.
The Indonesian government told Bre-X last week to negotiate a deal to give control of Busang to Barrick by today but the two companies said several points were unresolved.
"We're not discouraged. It's going to be a long process. I don't think today's deadline had any great signficance," Placer spokesman Hugh Leggatt said.
Placer had no response yet from the Indonesian government to its letter asking to be allowed to make a competing offer for Bre-X, he said.
